counting_conventions.dia-api: Distinct public/protected member names per export class in types/dia.d.ts; overloads collapsed; private excluded; inherited members counted on the declaring class only.
counting_conventions.paper-option: Declared fields of dia.Paper.Options in types/dia.d.ts; inherited mvc.ViewOptions fields excluded.
counting_conventions.event: Union of dia.Paper.EventMap keys, trigger() literals in src/**, and dynamic change:/eventPrefix patterns (flagged dynamic).
counting_conventions.link-anchor: Exported anchor names in src/linkAnchors/index.mjs (resolveRef helper excluded).
counting_conventions.link-tool: Top-level export class names in types/linkTools.d.ts.
counting_conventions.element-tool: Top-level export class names in types/elementTools.d.ts.
counting_conventions.layout-port: export var names under the Port namespace of types/layout.d.ts.
counting_conventions.layout-port-label: export var names under the PortLabel namespace of types/layout.d.ts.
counting_conventions.geometry: Distinct declared member names per export class in types/geometry.d.ts, plus standalone functions and bezier/scale/intersection namespace members.
counting_conventions.vectorizer: VElement member names plus VStatic members (prefix V.) in types/vectorizer.d.ts.
counting_conventions.util: export function/var names in types/util.d.ts, including timing/interpolate/filter/format namespace members.
counting_conventions.mvc: Distinct declared member names per export class in types/mvc.d.ts, plus Data and $ from src/mvc/index.mjs.
counting_conventions.presentation-attribute: Top-level keys of the attribute namespaces in src/dia/attributes/*.mjs, plus the props shorthand.
counting_conventions.core-config: Keys of src/config/index.mjs, plus env.addTest, env.test, setTheme, version.
counting_conventions.alg: The exported rightAnglePath function of types/alg.d.ts (upstream-flagged internal).
counting_conventions.package: Directories of packages/* in the monorepo carrying a package.json.
counting_conventions.package-api: Entry-point exports only, per package (see the enumerate.mjs header); @joint/core excluded.

entries.name: rightAnglePath
entries.behaviour: `alg.rightAnglePath` (upstream-flagged internal, consumed by @joint/router-avoid): given the two path ends with their bounding boxes, margins, and exit sides, it computes the right-angled path points between them, including any required detour around an end's box.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry scenario: run the same fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and through our implementation; assert the returned points or path samples match within 1e-6 world units (exact match for integer cases), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate (coincident points) case.

proof.note: No analogue in diagram-canvas; the README section at this line lists the uncovered areas.

entries.name: bottom
entries.behaviour: Element anchor `bottom`: given the end element (or port) geometry, the magnet, and the reference point, it computes the link end point on the element following the "bottom" rule. Moving or resizing the element moves the computed end point accordingly.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry scenario: run the same fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and through our implementation; assert the returned points or path samples match within 1e-6 world units (exact match for integer cases), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate (coincident points) case.

proof.note: diagram-canvas portAnchorPoint computes a side anchor point on an owner rect from a normalised position; JointJS anchors also handle magnets, rotation, percentages, and calc expressions, so the analogue is partial.

entries.name: anchor
entries.behaviour: Connection point `anchor`: given the link end segment and the end element's shape or bounding box, it trims or extends the rendered path end to the "anchor" boundary, so the visible path starts or ends exactly at the computed point.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry scenario: run the same fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and through our implementation; assert the returned points or path samples match within 1e-6 world units (exact match for integer cases), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate (coincident points) case.

proof.note: No analogue in diagram-canvas; the README section at this line lists the uncovered areas.

entries.name: cellDefaultsMergeStrategy
entries.behaviour: `config.cellDefaultsMergeStrategy`: a global JointJS setting. Reading or setting it changes the documented library-wide default (merging, selectors, theme, capability tests, or version reporting) for all subsequently created graphs, papers, and cells.
entries.acceptance: Differential unit scenario: run the same inputs through the JointJS helper and our replacement; assert deep equality of the returned values (exact for strings and integers, 1e-9 for floats), including one edge input (empty, missing, or boundary value). SVG-node cases compare the resulting serialised node, not the live DOM identity.

proof.note: No module owns this on our stack yet; a new module is required (see the spec).

entries.acceptance: Differential interaction scenario: build the same paper and scripted pointer or option sequence in JointJS and in our diagram-canvas plus renderer harness (playwright-core, headless Chrome); assert the emitted event sequence, the camera or scene result, and the model result match, with pointer coordinates compared after the shared world transform.

proof.note: No analogue in diagram-core; the README section at this line lists the uncovered areas.

entries.name: curveThroughPoints
entries.behaviour: `g.bezier.curveThroughPoints` (function): a pure plane-geometry operation. Given the documented geometric inputs, it returns the documented points, shapes, distances, intersections, or serialised form, with no rendering side effects.
entries.acceptance: Differential geometry scenario: run the same fixed inputs (boxes, points, vertices, options) through JointJS (@joint/core 4.3.3) and through our implementation; assert the returned points or path samples match within 1e-6 world units (exact match for integer cases), including one rotated-element case and one degenerate (coincident points) case.
